Subject: Re: Discovery — inference workloads & deployment modes

Thanks for the call, Marissa — appreciate the overview. A quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying items before we fill the workbook: 

Summary:
- Opsync is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing recommendation endpoint that will power real-time suggestions in our web product.
- Primary constraint: latency SLO of 200ms p95, daytime peak expected 4000 qps across shards (global), initial US rollout.
- Security: must support VPC peering and audit logs; SOC2 evidence requested.

Clarifying asks for sizing workbook:
1) Preferred GPU families: we have some flexibility but would like guidance if H100 vs A100 is recommended for a mixed token profile.
2) Typical token mix: prompts ~150–600 tokens, completions ~80–250 tokens; how does that affect concurrency and KV-cache sizing?
3) Does Redwood recommend Dedicated (reserved pools) for throughput predictability or should we start Hosted + burst into Dedicated?

Attached: our sample trace (small) and a simple latency matrix. I will get you fuller trace logs once I extract them from prod.

Next steps: please send the capacity workbook you mentioned and any rough ballpark for GPU counts given the TPS/latency above. Happy to schedule a 30-min follow-up with our infra lead.

— Samir
Platform Lead, Opsync

Subject: Post-call: deploy-mode recap & dedicated capacity sizing asks

Samir — thanks for the clear notes and for sharing the trace excerpt. Attaching the capacity_workbook_OPS-2026.xlsx and a short latency matrix we maintain for Redwood Dedicated. Below I put a quick playbook-style response and a couple of data requests that will let us size more precisely.

Redwood quick guidance (based on what you shared):
- Deployment mode: for a customer-facing recommendation endpoint with 4k peak qps and a hard 200ms p95 target, Dedicated is the simplest path to predictable latency. Hosted can work during evaluation but we'll likely recommend an initial Dedicated pool for predictable SLOs with autoscale/burst policies enabled. Private (VPC) is also possible once you need an air-gapped control plane.
- GPU family: H100 preferred for sustained high throughput + longer context (if you anticipate many 600-token prompts). A100S is cost-effective for shorter sequence averages.
- TPS / concurrency: to start ballpark — if your request profile averages 250 tokens total (prompt+completion) with batching enabled and smart KV caching, estimate ~350–450 token TPS per H100 (conservative). For 4k qps we need to map qps -> token TPS (example: 4k qps * 250 tokens = 1,000,000 token TPS). That implies ~3 H100s per 300k token TPS band (rough ballpark), so ~3–4 H100s to start with aggressive autoscale. We'll refine after you confirm token mix and exact p95 target under payload sizes.

Data we need from you (fill these into the workbook):
- Actual qps distribution (5/50/95 percentiles by hour)
- Representative request traces with prompt and completion token counts (10–100 samples across peak)
- Whether you use tool/function calling or external retrievals per request (adds latency variability)
- Preferred region and any hard GPU preferences or corporate discounts

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Samir — please complete the Capacity workbook tab "Workload inputs" and attach a small (zipped) trace CSV with columns: timestamp, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, latency_ms.
2) Aditya — will you take a first-pass dedicated sizing estimate (H100 vs A100) based on their stated token mix?
3) Lauren — can you prepare a one-pager on our Dedicated networking (VPC peering, private control plane) and SOC2 artifacts to send to Opsync's security team?
4) Samir — propose 30 min windows tomorrow or Thursday for a sizing sync with infra.

We can pivot to hosted for the POC if Opsync wants to avoid procurement during evaluation, but our recommended POC approach is: hosted for feature validation -> short Hosted->Dedicated ramp for stress testing -> Dedicated reserved once performance/SLAs validated.

Thanks — I’ll keep this thread updated as we get the workbook back.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: capacity_workbook_OPS-2026.xlsx, inference_latency_matrix.pdf

Quick sizing pass from my side (ballpark) — putting numbers so Opsync has something to work with in the workbook: 

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Peak qps: 4,000 requests/sec (burstable to 5k)
- Average tokens per request: 250 (prompt+completion)
- Batch window: 5–15ms continuous batching, KV caching for 65% of requests

Ballpark (conservative):
- Token TPS requirement: 4k * 250 = 1,000,000 token TPS
- Effective throughput per H100 (with batching & caching): ~350k token TPS -> ~3 H100s baseline
- Add 1–2 H100s for headroom and autoscale (4–5 total) depending on burst profile and failure domain requirements
- If you prefer A100 GPUs, plan +30–40% more GPUs for same throughput.

Concurrency guidance: aim to maintain per-GPU concurrency that keeps KV cache hit behavior high and avoids head-of-line blocking. We typically recommend configuring the Serving Pool with a concurrency cap and letting the autoscaler scale by tokens. I can sketch a sample autoscaling policy once we have percentiles.

I'll draft a quick example policy and drop into the Drive folder. If Opsync can share 1 hour of peak traces (CSV), I can produce a provisional perf run simulation.

— Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa and Aditya — this is very helpful. I filled out the top-level Workload inputs in the workbook and attached a small zipped sample traces.csv (10 rows) to the Drive link.

Answers inline:
- Token mix: median ~210 tokens, p95 ~480 tokens; we saw a lot of small completions (80–120 tokens) and a few heavy prompts at 500–600.
- Function/tool calling: yes, ~18% of requests call out to retrieval; those usually add 30–80ms depending on DB latency.
- Preferred region: us-west-2; procurement prefers A100 but engineering prefers H100 if cost allows.

I can do a 30-min sync Thu 10:00–10:30 or Fri 15:00–15:30 PT — Thu works best. In that sync I'd like you to:
- Walk through the provisional 4–5 H100 estimate and failure domain plan
- Show autoscale policy controls and how we can test headroom during POC
- Clarify when VPC/private control plane is needed vs starting with Dedicated in Redwood-managed control plane

If you can drop a short agenda here I’ll send calendar invite for Thu 10:00.

— Samir
